items.headline: The valuation read is being pulled by sentiment
items.detail: The composite sits at the 17th percentile, but the sentiment axis is at 68 while the rest average 23 — the one dimension running hot.
items.framing: Everything is cheap except sentiment, which reads 68/100. That divergence is the story — it's how the exchange-flow build-up first became visible.
items.checkable: Each axis is a percentile of its own history; published weights on the Methods page.

items.headline: Holders ~14% underwater — and still not selling
items.detail: MVRV 0.86: price is 14% below the crowd's avg on-chain cost basis ($0.499). Yet 58% of supply is in the longest-held tier — the float isn't moving.
items.framing: Maximum financial pain, minimal capitulation — conviction being tested and, so far, holding.
items.note: Describe the divergence, NOT a bottom call. "Not selling", not "buy".

items.headline: -81% below its all-time high
items.detail: Deepest drawdown on record was -95%; it has made new highs after every prior one so far.
items.framing: Deep drawdowns are the toll — it's paid them before (no recovery promise).
items.note: It's deep and unrecovered NOW; don't imply it always recovers.

items.headline: One wallet scooped 8 AEON over 2 days
items.detail: 0xb744…337d is the biggest net buyer of Project AEON over 30 days — 3.6 ETH ($9,596), well clear of the field.
items.framing: One wallet accumulated 8 AEON (~$9,596) on the market. Show the tornado / the city arcs — anyone can verify it.
items.checkable: Net marketplace buys minus sells per wallet over 30 days, from the public sale log.

items.headline: SPX's MVRV 0.86 = 7th percentile of Bitcoin's history
items.detail: SPX's MVRV of 0.86 sits at the 7th percentile of Bitcoin's entire MVRV history — as cheap as BTC's generational bottoms.
items.framing: MVRV is unitless, so it's comparable: SPX today is at BTC's 7th percentile. BTC was only this cheap at major bottoms.
items.note: A position on BTC's map, not a date-match forecast.

items.headline: -82% below its long-run trend (Fire Sale band)
items.detail: Fair value for its age is $2.39; price sits -82% under it.
items.framing: Where today sits in the long power-law arc.

items.headline: 80% of all-time holders are gone — 92% of today's never sold to zero
items.detail: Of 26,958 wallets that ever held ≥5k SPX, 5,358 remain (80% churned). Yet 92% of CURRENT holders have never once sold to zero — survivorship.
items.framing: Enormous all-time churn, but the survivors are diamond-handed. The honest "who's still here" read.
items.note: Right-censoring: recent cohorts read high. "Gone" = fell below the 5k bar.

items.headline: Smart money still net-selling (-16.4% over 12w)
items.detail: The 10-wallet cohort of proven top-timers (ROI ≥5×, still holding) holds 6.86M SPX. 4w -14.5% · 12w -16.4% · 26w -23.6%.
items.framing: Smart money hasn't started buying yet (-16.4% in 12w). Honest "not the bottom signal yet" read.
items.checkable: A recomputed cohort of wallets with realized ROI ≥5× that still hold ≥50k SPX; net flow of their combined balance.

items.headline: 1 new proven top-timer in 90 days
items.detail: Wallet(s) that just crossed the ROI+capital bar by selling a top at profit — a burst means distribution is starting.
items.framing: 1 wallet(s) newly qualified as smart money in 90d (sold a top at ≥5× ROI). Low count = quiet market; a spike is the tell.
items.checkable: First crossing of the ROI+capital bar per wallet, from the sale history.

items.headline: NUPL -0.17 — capitulation
items.detail: Net unrealised profit/loss is -0.17 (from MVRV 0.86) — the market sits in the capitulation zone.
items.framing: Aggregate holder profitability. Below zero = the crowd is underwater, historically an accumulation zone.
items.note: A position read, not a signal.

items.headline: The base is sitting tighter than usual
items.detail: Liveliness 0.610 is 1.6σ down vs its month. Rising = old coins moving (distribution/rotation); falling = holders sitting still (accumulation).
items.framing: Coins are sitting tighter — liveliness fell. The base is holding, dormancy deepening.
items.checkable: Coin-days-destroyed vs coin-days-stored from the FIFO reconstruction.

items.headline: A whale added 700k SPX in 7 days
items.detail: 0x446b…27ba accumulated over the window, one of 3 whales net-buying.
items.framing: A large wallet accumulated 700k SPX in 7 days. Real, checkable buying by a big holder.
items.checkable: Net balance change on a watched wallet over the last week of transfers.

items.headline: -1.2σ below its trend vs the alt market
items.detail: SPX ÷ the alt sector (ex-BTC/ETH/stables), detrended, sits 1.2σ below its own trend — cheap vs alts.
items.framing: Relative value vs the whole alt sector — -1.2σ cheap. SPX structurally outperforms alts, so this is deviation from ITS trend, not parity.
items.note: A relative-value position, not a signal.

items.headline: A whale shed 500k SPX in 7 days
items.detail: 0x3e71…611c distributed over the window.
items.framing: A large wallet distributed 500k SPX in 7 days. State it as a move off this wallet — it may be a split (see clustering), not a market sell.
items.checkable: Net balance change on a watched wallet over the last week of transfers.

items.headline: A 1.77M-SPX holder moved everything to a new wallet of its own
items.detail: 2026-09-26 (7d ago). A test send, a test sent back, then the whole balance — the coins keep their age and cost, so it is not a sale and books no profit or loss.
items.framing: A 1.77M SPX position changed wallets on 2026-09-26: same holder, new address. Say "moved to a new wallet", never "sold" or "exited".
items.checkable: The handshake (small send, small send back, then the balance) is in the raw transfer history; both wallets are linked below.

items.headline: 165× at this age — vs Ethereum's 78×
items.detail: At the same age since launch (~3yr), SPX6900 is 165× vs Ethereum's 78× at the same point in its life.
items.framing: History rhymes: at this age SPX is 165×, Ethereum was 78×. A same-age comparison, not a forecast.

items.detail: ETH 49,179 · Base 114,068 · Solana 73,253 = 236,500 wallets, +2.8% in ~30d. Base leads on headcount, ETH on value.
items.framing: The real reach: 236,500 wallets across three chains — most people on Base/Solana, most value on ETH.
items.note: Wallets, not people; Base/Solana are bridged.

items.headline: 65% of supply held over a year
items.detail: 65% of tracked supply hasn't moved in 12 months — the deep-conviction base, comparable to Bitcoin at the same age.
items.framing: A 65% one-year-plus base — the cohort that held through everything.
items.note: Coin age from the FIFO reconstruction.

items.headline: 51% of supply is in profit
items.detail: 51% of tracked supply is held above its on-chain cost basis — low is a capitulation zone, high is euphoria risk.
items.framing: Mid-range holder profitability.
items.note: A position read, not a signal.

items.headline: +4% since the last Fire Sale low (2026-09-29)
items.detail: Off the 2026-09-29 capitulation low ($0.413), price is +4%, having peaked +8%.
items.framing: Every capitulation-band low has rallied off it.
items.note: Pattern, not a promise; the chart shows the first 90 days.

items.headline: SOPR 1.015 — coins moving at a profit
items.detail: Spent-output profit ratio is 1.015: coins that moved on-chain realised a gain on average. Sustained <1 = capitulation, >1 = profit-taking.
items.framing: On-chain realised behaviour — profit-taking (SOPR 1.015).
items.note: Only coins that MOVED; a behaviour read, not a signal.

items.headline: 3.31M SPX left in a day
items.detail: 2026-10-01: 50 wallets dropped below the 5k bar with 3.31M SPX, 2.1σ above the usual churn — 83% in profit (profit-taking).
items.framing: A profit-taking exit wave — 50 wallets banked 3.31M SPX and stepped down. Holders selling strength, not fear; the honest hook is WHO takes profit and when.
items.checkable: Wallets whose balance fell below the 5k residency bar that day, split by exit vs entry price.

items.headline: Diamond share up +1.1pp → 41.8%
items.detail: 392,670,052 SPX now in the longest-held tier.
items.framing: Post it — ~9,976,658 SPX just aged into DIAMOND hands (the longest-held, rarely-sold tier). Coins reach it only by being HELD through everything, not by trading — supply maturing into strong hands, conviction deepening. Diamond hands earning the name.
items.note: Word it as HELD, not BOUGHT: the +9,976,658 came from a cohort aging in from gold (≈ gold -10,924,456), not fresh demand. "Held into diamond" ✓ · "diamonds bought 9,976,658" ✗.
